Subject: Hosted streaming chat - repeated disconnects during 7pm-9pm PST

Hi Sofia / Laura,

We're seeing repeated disconnects and very long responses from the hosted streaming chat endpoint during our evening peak (roughly 19:00-21:00 PST). p99 latency for SSE connections spikes above 6s and a non-trivial percentage of sessions drop mid-conversation. This started after the model config change you rolled last week (v1.3.2 -> v1.4.0). Our customers in CA are impacted—conversations time out and our front-end shows the spinner forever.

We've pulled a short metrics snapshot (attached) and a sample client trace. Can you confirm whether there are any autoscaling/resizing events on your side, or known regressions in the streaming runtime tied to v1.4.0? This is high priority for BrightMarket; our CSAT is already taking a hit.

Subject: RE: Hosted streaming chat - repeated disconnects during 7pm-9pm PST

Sofia / team — quick summary from preliminary checks:

- Observed pattern: p95 is stable ~400-600ms; p99 shows sudden step increases coincident with request bursts at 19:15/19:45/20:30 PST. The spikes align with high-concurrency prefix-heavy sessions from BrightMarket.
- Runtime: v1.4.0 introduced a change to token-prefetch batching + an altered KV cache TTL (shorter) to reduce memory. That change increases cache churn under very bursty prefix reuse patterns.
- Autoscaling: no obvious scale-downs; we saw brief throttling in the SSE worker pool on cluster eu-west-2-hosted-03 (internal routing attempt) — likely causing increased queueing.

Immediate hypothesis: increased KV cache misses + a hot-worker queueing effect -> amplified tail latency on a small subset of shards. End-to-end impact manifests as p99 spikes and occasional disconnects when the websocket SSE connection idle timers exceed the client threshold.

Actions taken:
- Pulled targeted logs and attached them (sse-debug-logs-20280930.zip).
- Temporarily bumped SSE worker pool concurrency on the impacted shard set (rolled 2/5 of the pool to a higher concurrency config). Observing dashboards now; early read shows p99 reduced ~15% on the patched shards.
- Reverting the TTL change is low-friction but requires a controlled rollout (can do canary for BrightMarket).

Next steps (ask to sales):
- Sofia, please let BrightMarket know we are actively mitigating and propose a canary rollback of the TTL change to v1.3.2 for their traffic window tonight.
- Laura, coordinate with CS for customer messaging and incident timeline.

I'll continue monitoring and will push further config updates if we don't see sustained improvement.

Marcus Lin
SE Lead — Hosted Runtime
